subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which prompt/tool-schema overhead reductions should this canonical tracker own next, and what plugin/API/config contract is acceptable for deferred or slim tool definitions?
rationale: The remaining fixes affect model prompt policy, provider contracts, plugin SDK expectations, channel action compatibility, and possible new config surfaces, so automation cannot choose the permanent product boundary safely.

options.title: Sequence compatible core reductions first
options.body: Keep #14785 canonical, land no-behavior-change prompt/schema reductions first, and require maintainer approval before adding new plugin SDK or config surfaces.

options.title: Narrow to Tool Search only
options.body: Treat existing Tool Search directory/code mode as the intended mitigation and split any remaining prompt/schema complaints into narrower follow-up issues.

options.title: Design a new deferred-tool API
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers approve a plugin-facing deferred schema or slim-schema API with explicit upgrade and provider compatibility rules.

recommendation.title: Sequence compatible core reductions first
recommendation.body: Keep #14785 canonical, land no-behavior-change prompt/schema reductions first, and require maintainer approval before adding new plugin SDK or config surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad prompt/tool-schema policy and most affected file history converge on steipete as the best available decision owner.
